title: Kenyan Avocado Toast
community: Urban Kenya — the millennial Nairobi breakfast
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Avocado Toast — thick-sliced toasted sourdough topped with smashed Kenyan avocado, kachumbari, chilli flakes, a squeeze of lemon, fresh coriander, and a fried egg. The global breakfast trend made better with Kenya's world-class avocados.
longDesc: Kenya produces some of the world's finest avocados — the large, buttery Hass and Fuerte varieties that grow in the highlands have an extraordinary richness and flavour. On good sourdough with kachumbari and a fried egg, Kenyan avocado toast surpasses versions made with avocados imported from anywhere else.
ingredients: 4 thick slices sourdough or good bread
steps: Toast bread until golden and crispy.
Mash avocados with lime juice, salt, and pepper. Keep some texture.
Spread avocado generously on each toast.
Fry or poach eggs to preference.
Spoon kachumbari on top of the avocado.
Scatter chilli flakes, coriander, and a drizzle of olive oil.
Finish with flaky salt. Serve immediately.
chefTips: The avocado must be perfectly ripe — Kenyan avocados are at their best when the skin gives slightly under gentle pressure.
Add lime juice immediately after mashing — prevents browning.
Drained kachumbari is key — excess liquid makes the toast soggy.
cookingScience: See KEN138 for avocado browning science. Draining kachumbari removes tomato water that would otherwise saturate the toast — keeping the base crispy under the avocado layer.
sustainabilityTips: Kenyan avocados consumed locally have zero food miles.
Kenya is a major avocado exporter — buying locally grown reduces the carbon footprint dramatically.
healthBenefits: Rich in healthy monounsaturated fats from avocado.
Kachumbari adds vitamins C and lycopene.
High in potassium — more than a banana.
culturalNote: Kenyan avocado toast represents Nairobi's thriving modern café scene claiming this global breakfast trend with confidence — Kenya's avocados make a genuinely superior version of this dish that locals and visitors alike recognise.
